public_payload.normalized_proposition: Scaling performance by training models longer is no longer really holding.

statement.excerpt: The new version is that there is not one scaling law, but three: scaling with how long you train a model (which isn’t really holding anymore), scaling with how long you post-train a model, and scaling with how long you let a given model wrestle with a given problem (or what Satya Nadella called scaling with “inference time compute”).
statement.document_title: The new AI scaling law shell game

from_speaker: scaling with how long you train a model
our_interpretation: Assess the parenthetical claim about pretraining, rather than the separate enumeration of three scaling approaches.
The plain reading is that increasing pretraining scale no longer reliably delivers the capability gains previously expected. It need not mean that every additional training step produces no benefit.
The surrounding last-few-weeks discussion places the current state in November 1–24, 2024. Older experiments provide context only.
Training duration is read in the surrounding context of pretraining compute, model size and data, rather than wall-clock time alone.
criteria.support_condition: Comparable predictions and measured frontier pretraining results for the claimed period show systematic shortfalls in expected capability gains.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Comparable predictions and measured results for that period show that increasing pretraining scale continued reliably to deliver the expected gains.
